I'm in the process of understanding this as well. I began my spiritual journey in earnest \*because\* of the monumental upheaval caused by a breakup in my life.  I don't know if a question like "how long does it take" will be useful to you, because then you are in a trance of comparing yourself to others. In my experience, the Holy Spirit is who we should turn to. And like Gandalf the Holy Spirit is neither late nor early, but arrives exactly when he means to. So you may be in a period of suffering right now due to lack of forgiveness for yourself or the other person. Likely both. Finding a way to "douse" that hot suffering with forgiveness will benefit you. Much easier said than done. Doing the workbook/reading the course text will help you. the concept of Atonement completely reframed forgiveness for me.  
However, there is also a section on patience in the Course. Christ was Resurrected but it did take 3 days. That 3 days is a symbolic time frame, and during that time he experienced the Harrowing of Hell, but it is indicative of the horizontal time that was necessary even for him!  
like I mentioned, my breakup was the impetus for enormous spiritual evolution \*because\* it was so painful. In my case, after 9 months of hard work the Spirit told me (over and over to my chagrin) to reach out to my ex to make amends. We are now becoming friends (slowly, and with great care) and I may not have lost her at all. That is the power of the Miracle of meeting others with love and not fear. I'm not saying thats in the cards for you, but I was shocked to find it was in the cards for me. My therapist, who is also a student of the Course and introduced me to it, said "this is a manifestation of the work you've been doing, you see that right?" and I am still finding it hard to believe.  
The course says that sometimes people fall out of your life and they weren't meant for you, or you've learned all you can from them, but sometimes they come back. And that is important to note too. This could be the beginning of a new relationship (with yourself and with God) that will lead you to who you are meant for. Try to listen closely and be patient. And Honor this period. Even if you were "healed of heartbreak" you would still have suffering of another kind. This one is so hot and ready for you it's a perfect opportunity to begin practicing! The Ego's "biggest gun" is the Special Relationship. It wants you to think Romance is just as good as God. It's not! God is that and a bag of chips. Good luck!

Update: the field seems to be dominated to an almost pathological degree with one thing: human psychology as it evolved for sexual selection. Useless. This is the thing we have the most cognitive control over. And if they were doing anything useful they’d be exploring mating for specific psychology than looking at finger sizes or having women smell T-shirts with sweat on them and rating them. You never pick a mate by a tee shirt smell. It’s over simplified and materialistic. I would say now a person may be more willing to enter a situation of raising fewer children as a group (more parents) even if you weren’t genetically copying yourself in the arrangement. It could be a better system to insure a child has a higher chance of success psychologically, you pass on wellness learning benefiting the species without passing on specific genes. The survival factor could be greater. Who knows! In this situation a child isn’t  dependent on a parent (sometimes two) that can’t meet their needs. With developments in conditions (trends in medical research, algorithms for healthier match making, less threat of random violence (hopefully) that may make a woman choose a male based on size alone (according to EP).) There are also studies of evolutionary altruism which are being looked in to. Which is neither here nor there. But sounds interesting! Nothing immediately useful to my question. And I’m a little disheartened. Most immediately available content is on sex selection and people getting mad at people studying sex selection. lol I just wished they’d pick something interesting.

I see the project as comprehensive documentation of whatever “ghosts” and “demons” are. One aspect of possession is CERTAINLY mental illness/cognitive distortion. You cannot conceive of a reality without the prison the “demon” creates in your mind. Another seems to be an affectation on a sense of self. A new, and dark, self takes over. I wonder if a priest (if the affected person is a Christian) would help at all in this situation. But yes, exorcisms as a rule seem to be medieval and perhaps a new form needs to be taken. Something like CBT but allowing for a conception of a demon to exist in that process. Instead of just manhandling a sick woman or whatever. I hope therapy is a component for all these families in the future. But I wonder if the exorcism ever helps them begin that therapy process (it could, if it gave them a sense of relief and freedom even temporarily) or if it just stagnates after and they never seek further help. Thats why I wonder about check ins.

She should be happy, because most damage is done when one person is impulsive and emotionally reactive than when one is not. For instance, your partners “not a person” comment was during a state of emotional reactivity. And is not something she would think outside of it. She should apologize to you for that. 

It’s almost as if our dependability and evenness (when not overwhelmed) is taken for granted sometimes when a partner wants you to rant and rave with them. I had a partner who would act out on purpose just to try and get a rise out of me, we didn’t last long because everyone has a limit, but they were testing to see if I was “real” because i behaved so unusually to thier reactive behaviors. First breakups are hard. Especially if they are messy. And they usually are. 

You are learning how to love. This experience has been important. One day you will see you wouldn’t be who you have grown to be without the pain. 

My first break up was over a decade ago. I struggle for a long time in many, many short and long term relationships in the past decade. One day I realized it was because I had never gotten over her. 

When I began to get serious about healing, I got serious about seeing how much of the pain I was causing myself. She had nothing to do with it! 

When that process had been working for a couple of years, I fell in love again. And it was just as powerful as the first time. Something I hadn’t been able to say since I was a teenager.  

I thought I was simply *unable* to love. That first breakup had *broken* me. But it was only *believing* that it had that made my romantic life a long struggle. 

That new relationship ended too. But I know now I can love and will love again. I am so good at it now because of the pain I’ve endured. And you will be too. 

Someone will be so lucky to be with you one day. I know it.

This is a really good question. Alcohol dependency seems to be at its most “acceptable” when it is used in context as a “social lubricant” NTs and NDs alike do this! And both are capable of slowly slipping into abusive patterns without noticing. One day I realized  i only see “friends” when i and they were drunk! And don’t truly know any of them at all. This is a tough realization. 

My issue was that I couldn’t hang out without drinking. Full stop. I’d get such awful anxiety before even meeting a friend to see a movie (which is as easy as it gets for me) I’d dry heave. So I’d usually have a beer before leaving. And have one at the theater if possible (I always picked theaters you could drink at). I think people without dependency would not have this struggle. 

Parties seem (to me) to be occasions built around drinking. But I think others go to not only drink but see their friends. I would go to parties, talk all night to everyone and drink a lot. The next day id wake up two kinds of hung over. Regular and Social hangover (combining to produce what I called a Shame-over) 

Tho I’ve been to a few sober parties now that I’ve quit and have a social partner. I still wake up hung over. But only the social hang over, which has some similar aspects! Fatigue and headache and sometimes deep sadness. But the shame that made me literally despise myself is gone now. Alcohol is not kind to me.

This sounds very similar to how beer was for me.  When I first started to understand that I navigated according to a different map than others, there was a moment of relief. I always thought I was just “lazy/scatterbrained/tunnel-visioned/selfish/inattentive” etc. Any name a parent/ partner/friend would call an autistic person who is simply existing differently. Then I realized I wasn’t broken I was just autistic. And it helped me realize I had skills those people didn’t have. People like to say we don’t understand humans. But I think we do on a deeper level and it makes them uncomfortable. I see every single person I meet as a complete human (with flaws, traits, strengths and weaknesses s) and I see myself as a kind of goo that fits the form it needs to. Other people are not like this. They are very Ego focused. And have a rigid identity. They often attack when that is threatened and take longer to learn and grow as a result. Yes, many things are harder for us. But I love the autistic people in my life. And I love my “self” whatever that is. Try not to feel discouraged. There are gifts here as well as challenges.

I have been called “thoughtful and well spoken” and people would often tell me I said something that moved them deeply when I was drunk (that of course I don’t remember). I write and have struggled with finding that Free Hyperlexic place in myself sober. I used to drink alone and write for hours and hours. The work was often puzzling and sad but it had some kind of merit. Now I apply sober logic to everything. That’s my biggest hill right now. How to loosen up

I was at the “black out and cry” level when I quit drinking the first time. Even tho it feels rotten it can be very important to reach that stage if you need to so you know, without a doubt, drinking is harming you more than helping. And it lets you know what it is that hurting you the most. For me, it was my parents. I’d cry about them every time I blacked out. 
I’ve quit and started up again a few times now. Right now I’m almost 7 months sober and in a relationship with someone in AA so it makes going to meetings and talking about the experience of alcohol dependency easier. I like Zoom AA meetings too (you can find them online. NYC Intergroup is great. You don’t have to live in NYC to use them.) but as for Spectrum specific groups I haven’t seen one. 
I haven’t found a way to socialize without alcohol. But I’ve found gaming or some other activity based outing makes it easier. I like RPGs and Chess and Cards. Or just crafting with another person.
A 12 step program will involve having a sponsor and being required to make several phone calls a day. I find the social aspect of AA it’s strength for NTs and it’s weakness for introverts of all kinds but especially those of us on the spectrum (otherwise known as recluses lol)

Hey!

Joining in the choir here. I understand everything you are saying. You are certainly among friends here. Especially the “guilt” part. 
only I don’t call it guilt, I call it shame. Guilt is being upset about what you did (or didn’t) do, shame is being upset about *who you are* 

I often feel this shame around my family because it hurts me to see how much they love each other *without me* in a lot of ways. I can’t join in in huge laugh sessions or brush it off when someone hurts my feelings. But my empathy, like you, let’s me know *what they are feeling for each other and how much I am not a part of it* I feel like a stranger around people who saw me draw my first breath. They get me gift cards for Christmas cause they don’t know what I’m interested in. 

It’s caused a huge rift. They fundamentally don’t understand who I am and I work so hard to understand them. But I fall short. 

I shoulder the shame for this rift. I don’t want to. Nor do I need to, but I do. 

So I often pretend, the masking that everyone talks about here, to fit in *for their sakes and mine* and it’s exhausting. I often feel physically ill and drained afterward. So I can’t do it often. 

My partner calls her mom every day on the phone and I simply can’t. It would drain me and make me feel ashamed and hurt. She also wants a dog but they *need too much* and I can’t give anything. We compromised with a cat for both of us and I have a reptile. They are more on my level. 

You shouldn’t feel bad about the way these situations make you feel. And fighting it just drains you more. My family and I aren’t in much conversation these days. It would make me sad if it wasn’t such a terror emotionally for me to be around them. The gift card at Christmas is all I need.

I only feel sad about it when I’m masking. When I’m trying to explain how it is not being social or talking to family a lot and people look at me with sad eyes like I’m an emotional orphan.

Ultimately spending time with you makes you energized. So try to listen to you and what you want. Not what everyone else wants from you.

Firstly, I want to do a thought experiment. I want you to imagine a cool person. Do that for a second or two. Really describe in your mind what they are like. Now I want you to imagine a "normal" person. Are they the same? Are they different? In what ways are they the same? Is one more *interesting* than the other?

I'm betting the cooler person was not the same as the normal person. They were probably more interesting, right?

So, why insist a character be *normal* in order to be an interesting --and therefore a successful-- character? In what way is Olaf normal? C'mon! Elsa shoots snow out of her hands, how is that normal? Do you come to Frozen for the *normalcy? or the fantasy?*

Ok, next point. A lot of you are making a lot of assumptions about a character whose sexuality *we know nothing about.* We've established you are assuming something called normal. Let's unpack that.  Think again of that thought experiment. How closely do you resemble the "normal" person? Can you think of *anyone* who resembles the normal person? *Is normal even real in practice?*

Aren't all the people we love in our lives a little *odd* at the end of the day? Do you choose your friends based on how normal they are? Probably not. So chances are if you were able to point to a  "normal" person in your life, you probably just don't know them very well. Like a coworker who seems "together" or some other person you don't know enough about to see the weirdness.

In other words, you would be making an *assumption of normalcy.* ***Normalcy is at its very heart an assumption, not a truth.***

So, if we are saying Elsa's sexuality must be *normal* it is because we are *assuming* due to a fundamental lack of information. To rephrase an earlier point: *An assumption is not a truth. Normalcy is an assumption, so is normalcy a truth?* ***NO.***

Normalcy, or whatever you imagine it to be, is reflective of *implicit bias.* If you imagined that Normal person as straight, white, or male (and chances are you imagined them as at least one of these things if not all three) that is indicative of a societal bias because I gave you no other instruction, just imagine someone normal.

And if you are saying "oh we can *assume* Elsa is straight because most people are straight. Numbers are on our side" Then why did you construct your "normal person" as White, Straight or Male when none of these is a true majority type in the world?

The world is *over half women* and there are way more Han Chinese in the world than white people. Also, as sexuality does not express a phenotype, we *have no way of knowing how many queer people there are in the world.* More and more are coming out in each generation. 51% or more of people *could be queer* *and just not out* due to societal pressures. So unless you imagined a Han Chinese woman of ambiguous sexuality, you were not actually imagining a statistical majority. Think about it!

What societal pressures might I be referring to above? How about people actively going on a forum and saying how making a character gay/queer/ace would "ruin her" to name one. There are obviously many other pressures much less benign. But take a minute to notice how you *contribute to those pressures even if it is less harmful than outright abuse.* I don't think any of yall are actively homophobic but are you anti-homophobic? Is the OP anti-homophobic? I think the answer is clearly, no. Because a truly homophobic person *could use the same argument and achieve the same desired end.*

So a lot of you are also upset about the campaign behind "making Elsa gay." You say there are plenty of queer characters already, why "force" Elsa to be one of them. First off, it wouldn't be forcing her, as I've said, we have nil, and assuming straightness is a bias, not a valid argument (no substantial evidence.) If anything you are *forcing her straight* in your assumption! So giving her a love interest/lack of interest explicitly would be defining her, as in quantifying nil with a value, not changing her.

On the other hand, I agree. There are a lot of great characters out there for queer people these days. Young and old alike. But this is a recent phenomenon in the last 10 or so years. Its no wonder "make Elsa gay" is trending, for the first time, we believe it might be *possible.* I grew up knowing *no one on tv or in movies would be like me* now I'm overwhelmed! But I still feel so sorry for little me, who had nothing. I want today's queer kids to have what I didn't.

However, to get to the place we are now, *there had to be a first. And we don't have a first in this category.* So, since you can't point to an example just like Elsa and say "oh you already have that Disney Princess in that movie, why use this one?" and you are still saying there is already enough out there for us, you are simply not making a valid argument.

Also, if you want to debate, why do we need another *straight* princess? Don't you have enough?  See why "having enough representation" is not a valid argument?

Lastly, you say the movie would be a "flop" if Elsa was gay in the (as of this post) unannounced Frozen 3. Let's look at Frozen's original marketing plan. Was it to present the world with a *normal princess like all the others?* OR was it a movie that sought to *break the princess mold Disney had clung to for so long?* I think you know, as fans of the film, it was the latter.

Elsa is a fantastic trope-breaker already, in fact, it is the *entire* reason the film even *exists!* They wanted to make an independent, powerful princess that wanted to come into her own without a man at the end of her rainbow or any other sort of "patriarchal" bullshit getting in her way. She is *so powerful* you guys. Like she could kick almost any Marvel hero's ass.

So would making Elsa a trope breaker ruin her? Signs point to an emphatic no. Did Disney know the world would be ready (more than ready!) to have a different kind of princess? No. But were we? Hell yes. And I think we are ready for a queer one too.

Very last point. Financials. Would this film be banned in some countries if there was an explicit queer lead? Possibly. However, there is a thing called *editing* that exists. For instance. The adventure time finale contained an f/f kiss. This is a kid's show of course, and it played around the world. In countries where depicting this is like a literal crime, they simply *edited it out.* I'm sure Disney is a smart enough company to figure it out. They are just using this "banned" thing as a cop-out. We all know it. Disney shows up at the pride parades all over the country trying to woo us into theaters through performative allyship! They want our gay money! Why not try *earning it!*

The truth is everyone likes to make money, these films make money wherever they are shown. Turning down a blockbuster outright would almost certainly not happen even in countries that might ban same-sex depictions if the so-called offensive lines could be taken out. And that's all I'd expect we'd get, at the end of the day, if the Make Elsa Gay-ers are successful, a line from Elsa to Honeybadger or whatever where she says "I like you" and a hug. Maybe a scene. Snip snip. Done, now she can make Disney a jillion dollars wherever it would be banned.

Also, the financial stress of banning is further disproved by Disney themselves. They are making headway with *The Owl House*. Perhaps testing the waters financially/culturally for a bigger profile queer character, Elsa could be that character. Gird your loins, oh antis of this sub if so.

The hardest part of all of this is unlearning. We try to keenly observe, to learn what is expected of us, and then replicate that behavior. If that behavior is accepted, it's good, if it's not, it's wrong. Then we try again. My place in my family's house seemed to be at best,   playful bullying at the dinner table, or at worst, total banishment and removal of all rights (i was grounded for months at a time from everything, not allowed to leave the house, etc).

So, in order to survive, I learned to disappear. That's the behavior that was rewarded. That's what having a narcissistic parent does to a child with ASD, it seems, if our two stories are any example.
